findings.claim: In November 2005, more than ten years ago, a San Mateo County court approved Ellison's settlement of a shareholder derivative suit alleging insider trading in his sale of about $900 million of Oracle stock in January 2001. He agreed to give $100 million to charity in Oracle's name and pay $22 million in legal fees; the report records no admission of wrongdoing.

Oracle shareholders alleged in a derivative suit that Ellison, a co-founder and large holder in both companies, forced Oracle to overpay for NetSuite in 2016. After trial the Court of Chancery ruled for the defendants in 2023, finding the special committee's negotiation untainted by his influence, and the Delaware Supreme Court affirmed in January 2025.

In September 2022 the SEC found that Oracle subsidiaries in Turkey, the UAE and India used off-book slush funds in 2016 to 2019 to bribe foreign officials, and Oracle paid over $23 million without admitting or denying the findings. It was Oracle's second FCPA resolution, after a 2012 case over Oracle India.

In 2024 Oracle agreed to pay $115 million to settle a federal class action (Katz-Lacabe v. Oracle America) alleging it captured, compiled and sold people's online and offline data without consent. Oracle denies the allegations and any wrongdoing, and agreed to stop capturing certain user data.

Business Insider reported in May 2023 that Ellison had given about $35 million to Opportunity Matters Fund, a super PAC backing Senator Tim Scott: $5 million in October 2020 and about $30 million in 2021 and 2022, over three-quarters of what the PAC raised. He also gave $5 million to a pro-Rubio super PAC in 2016.

TheWrap reported in July 2025, citing an FCC order on the Skydance–Paramount merger, that Ellison would hold a minority voting interest of about 35.5% in the combined company, with his son David as CEO. In December 2025 he gave an irrevocable personal guarantee for $40.4 billion of equity financing for Paramount's bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, owner of CNN.

A September 2025 investigation by Democracy for Sale and Lighthouse Reports said Ellison's foundation has donated or pledged at least £257m to the Tony Blair Institute since 2021, without saying how much was paid. Former staff said the institute pushed Oracle technology to governments; it states there is no suggestion of illegality, and the institute denies advocating for Oracle.

IRS filings summarised by ProPublica show the Larry Ellison Foundation, with Ellison as sole director, disbursed about $76.4 million in 2024, $54.7 million in 2023 and $45.2 million in 2022. The summary does not name recipients.

In January and February 2026 investors filed two proposed class actions over Oracle's AI data-centre spending: a bondholder suit in New York state court naming Ellison among the defendants, alleging offering documents hid planned borrowing, and a securities suit in Delaware federal court. These are allegations; no liability has been found.

politics.reason: Major Republican donor: about $35 million in 2020–2022 to a super PAC backing Senator Tim Scott, as reported by Business Insider. Set to hold a minority voting interest of about 35.5% in the merged Paramount Skydance, and personally guaranteed $40.4 billion of equity for its bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, owner of CNN. His foundation has donated or pledged at least £257m to the Tony Blair Institute, amount paid not stated; no illegality is alleged.

social.reason: Oracle agreed in 2024 to pay $115 million to settle a class action alleging it collected and sold people's data without consent; it denies wrongdoing. Other labour and market-power concerns are not sourced here.

legal.reason: Oracle paid more than $23 million in 2022 to resolve SEC charges that subsidiaries bribed foreign officials, its second FCPA resolution. In 2005 Ellison agreed to give $100 million to charity in Oracle's name and pay $22 million in fees to settle a shareholder suit alleging insider trading; no admission was reported. Delaware courts ruled for him in 2023 and 2025 in a suit over Oracle's NetSuite purchase.

unresolved.reason: Investor class actions filed in early 2026 allege Oracle misled investors about its AI data-centre spending and borrowing; Ellison is named in the bondholder suit. These are allegations and no ruling on them was found.

proposal.counterweights: The Larry Ellison Foundation disbursed about $76 million in 2024 and $55 million in 2023, per its IRS filings.
proposal.rationale: Politics 1→2: tens of millions to one super PAC plus a large voting stake in Paramount meet 'major donor, owner of influential media'; 3 is arguable if the reviewer weighs the TBI reporting. Social 1→2: a $115m consumer privacy settlement. Legal 0→1: SEC FCPA penalty; the 2005 personal settlement involved no finding of liability, though a reviewer could read it as level 3. The NetSuite ruling went his way and adds nothing. Unresolved 0→2: pending company suits; Ellison is a named defendant in one, which could support 3.
